summary: Lighthouse on Hawkins Island at the mouth of Peninsula Harbour, Lake Superior, beside Marathon, Ontario. Lit 1891; the 1891 tower was later lost to fire; the present steel tower dates from 1975.

structures.type: square wooden tower with attached dwelling
structures.note: 56 ft to the vane, per the 1891 report

structures.type: square wooden tower with dwelling (replacement after fire)
structures.note: 39 ft. Demolition disputed: LF gives 1975; Rowlett says destroyed after deactivation in 1957
Rowlett gives 13 m (43 ft) and the year 1975; CCG list gives 12.8 m

access.note: LighthouseFriends advises the modern light is best seen by boat.

events.note: Wooden tower and dwelling, contract let 1890 to Charles Mickler of Collingwood
Put in operation for the first time on 1 August 1891
Hand fog horn established at the station in the fiscal year ended 30 June 1903 (the report's own period)
Chartered steamer Neepawah ran ashore in fog near Peninsula Harbour; supplies transferred to another boat
New catoptric light placed in the lantern room on 25 August 1914; four flashes at three-second intervals every 25 seconds; petroleum vapour illuminant
Mercury float and pedestal, quadruple flash reflectors and clockwork added; group of four flashes every 20 seconds
White square wooden dwelling and tower built to replace the lighthouse destroyed by fire; 39 ft tall
Electric fog trumpet, one-second blast every 15 seconds
Keeper Harry O'Conner found dead inside the lighthouse after a bottle note reached Marathon; rescue party sent to Hawkins Island
Fog typhon (diaphone) replaced the fog trumpet; two-second blast every 20 seconds
Keeper Edward Huard and helper Joseph Archibald pulled from Lake Superior by the crew of the Marathon Paper Mill tug Allagash after their small boat capsized

Island light renamed Hawkins Island Light and its characteristic changed from a white flash every 30 seconds to every 4 seconds; Peninsula Harbour Light moved to a new mast at the SW end of the peninsula; diaphone moved to a building beside the mast
Lighthouse Directory: the 1929 lighthouse was destroyed after being deactivated in 1957 (disputes LF's 1975 demolition date)
Second (1929) lighthouse demolished, per LF (disputed; see 1957)
Present steel skeleton tower, dated 1975 by the Lighthouse Directory
Skeletal tower with slatwork daymark seen displaying a flashing white light every four seconds

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's conflict (a source says the structure is gone, OSM maps one today) resolves this way: the structure LighthouseFriends reports demolished in 1975 was the 1929 replacement lighthouse. The steel skeleton tower standing today is listed by the CCG (entry 1106) and was seen in 2021.
The Lighthouse Directory dates the present steel tower to 1975; LighthouseFriends dates the demolition of the 1929 lighthouse to 1975. The two dates refer to different structures.

LighthouseFriends (cite 1) gives demolition in 1975; the Lighthouse Directory (cite 8) says the 1929 lighthouse was destroyed after being deactivated in 1957. The sources disagree; the story states both and does not resolve it.

The record's name Peninsula Harbour Light was the island light's name to 1962. From 1963 the CCG list names the island light Hawkins Island (entry 1106) and Peninsula Harbour Light is a mast light on the peninsula.

notes_for_editor: The 1909 keeper table (report p. 170, scan 177) prints the name 'T). R. TTawWins' (D. B. Hawkins) and the appointment date 'Aug. 31,1891' in separate blocks; both were matched by position and then checked on the page image, where the row reads Peninsula Harbour, D. B. Hawkins, Aug. 31, 1891, 555.00. The 1911 list (p. 248, scan 255) pairs 'Peninsula Harbour' with 'J. Blondin' in adjacent OCR text; the page image confirms the row (Peninsula Harbour, J. Blondin, Oct. 14, 1910). The story does not use the 1910 date. No primary source in the corpus covers the keepers from 1917 to 1953: marine_ca ends with fiscal 1923-24 and its station lists do not name the station after 1916, so those names rest on LighthouseFriends alone and should be checked against Canadian keeper lists if they can be reached. The LF body says 'David D. Coveney' and the LF keeper list says 'David E. Coveney'; the 1913 Marine certificate list has a 'David Edward Coveney' as a candidate. No source connects him to this station, so he is not linked. The fire that destroyed the original tower is undated in every source read. The 1891 facts (contract, cost, dimensions, first lighting 1 August 1891) come from the 1891 report as quoted by LighthouseFriends; the 1891 report is not in the corpus (marine_ca starts 1900), so these are second-hand. The 1891 report gives visibility as '16 miles' without naming the mile; the story keeps the report's wording. The CCG remarks read 'Seasonal (in place year round)' and the story quotes them without interpreting. Record check: the record's tower height of 13.0 m (OSM) and the CCG's 12.8 m differ slightly; the record's coordinates match the CCG and LF positions. Naming question for a human: the record calls the station Peninsula Harbour Light, the name used to 1962; the CCG now calls the island light Hawkins Island. Not checked: Parks Canada and the Directory of Federal Heritage Designations (no heritage designation is stated in the story). Newspaper searches (Chronicling America) for the station, the 1908 grounding, the 1949 bottle note and the 1953 capsizing returned no pages. Access: the Lighthouse Directory says the island is accessible only by boat, the site is open and the tower closed; the story says so in Today. The 1929 lighthouse's end is disputed (LighthouseFriends: demolished 1975; the Lighthouse Directory: destroyed after deactivation in 1957); both are stated in the story and neither is resolved here. The 1903 fog horn is dated to the report's fiscal year ended 30 June 1903, not the calendar year. The 1880s railway date rests on the Marathon & District Historical Society page, which dates its own timeline to 1885 and notes that its dates are still being checked.
